title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 14 — drop the eleven automated.stale markers objectui 0b36ffa repaired, re-read at the console pin 616df6598b42
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 14 of the 18.0 sweep's wave anchor. Round 6 (PR #24697) marked eleven checklist items `automated.stale` because their objectui live specs were red or skipped at the console pin. objectui#13132 repaired those specs, and it landed as objectui `0b36ffa` (pointer `6284006658` on the anchor). PR #24829 then moved `.objectui-sha` to `616df6598b42`, which contains `0b36ffa`. This PR removes the eleven markers.

Only ledger text changes, in `platform-core.json` (1 item), `records-forms.json` (8) and `studio-authoring.json` (2). Each edited item gets one `revision` bump and one `history` row. Each row names the pointer `6284006658`, objectui `0b36ffa` and the pin `616df6598b42`. There is no product code, test, pin, objectui spec, changeset or `RUNNER.md` change. After this PR, no item in any area file carries `automated.stale` (11 before, 0 after).

The history rows were committed with the placeholder `#PENDING-24579R14`, because a row's `ref` names this PR and the PR had no number yet. A follow-up commit on this branch swaps in this PR's number and changes nothing else.

## How each verdict was read

Every verdict comes from the spec's bytes, not from the pointer's wording.

- **objectui history.** I used a full, non-shallow read-only clone of objectui; the local checkout is shallow.
  - `merge-base --is-ancestor 0b36ffa 616df6598b42` → exit 0.
  - Control: `12dc7b47c340` is an ancestor of `0b36ffa` → exit 0.
  - Reverse: `616df6598b42` is an ancestor of `0b36ffa` → exit 1.
- **The pin at BASE.** `.objectui-sha` at BASE `41646a5788` is `616df6598b429d2b3687301a2041198928e68971`.
- **What changed in `e2e/live/`.**
  - Between the old pin `12dc7b47c340` and the new pin `616df6598b42`: 11 specs modified, all by objectui#13132, plus one new spec (`declared-sharing-rules-reach-13091.spec.ts`) that no item here cites.
  - Between `0b36ffa` and `616df6598b42` (10 commits): nothing in `e2e/live/`. So each repaired spec has the same blob at `0b36ffa` and at the new pin. Each also has the same blob at the old pin and at `0b36ffa`'s parent, so the only change is #13132's.
- **Live evidence.** The only live reading is objectui's own: the whole live suite measured 61 passed (11.0m) at `0b36ffa`, on the shipped showcase. That is objectui's measurement at `0b36ffa`, not a run at `616df6598b42`. No live run exists at the new pin, so the verdict there is **NOT MEASURED**. Ten objectui commits between `0b36ffa` and the pin touch product source, `app-shell`, `plugin-list` and `plugin-grid` among it, so green at `0b36ffa` does not carry over to the pin.
- **Rule applied.** A spec that loses its stale marker keeps only the clauses its ref (or the stale record's `runnerRule`) already claimed for it. I re-read each one against what it asserts at the new pin. Where it asserts less, the ref narrows and says so. Nothing widens.

## Per item

Every edited item loses `automated.stale` and gains one `history` row; the table names every other field changed.

**The retired case.** `user-filters`' lookup quick-filter case was deleted at `0b36ffa` because the shipped showcase declares no lookup user filter. The one item whose record cited it, `list-view-capabilities` (its stale `why`), no longer cites it, and its ref names the case as retired. No clause in any item rested on it. `adhoc-filter-sort-builder` counted it only inside "4 of 6 cases".

**`screen-flow` (named "unchanged" in the pointer).** Its blob is `6713a1875a8e` at all three shas. No item in these three files cites it, so there is no marker to judge.

## Items left alone

In the three claimed files:

- `studio-authoring.custom-page-render-and-blocks` mentions "user-filters" as a product feature (`acceptance[4]`), not the spec or its retired case.
- `records-forms.crud-roundtrip`, `form-view-gallery`, `concurrent-edit-conflict` and `conditional-rules-grid`, and `studio-authoring.first-run-loop`, cite a repaired spec but carry no `automated.stale`, so they are outside the claim (see Acceptance notes for two of them).

Outside the three files:

- `attachments-storage.inline-grid-receipt-cells` (`grid-file-upload`) and `automation.screen-flow-roundtrip` (`screen-flow`) carry no `automated.stale`.
- `cli.json`, `access-security.json`, `approvals.json` and `RUNNER.md` are excluded by the claim.

## Mechanism hypotheses

1. **"Every item's stale specs are among the pointer's repaired specs, so every `stale` block goes." Holds.** The stale records name 10 distinct specs, and all 10 are in the pointer's repaired list. All 11 blocks go.
2. **"The pointer's spec names map one-to-one onto the specs the stale records cite, `studio-editor` a twelfth row that may appear in no item." Partly falsified.**
   - Of the pointer's 11 repaired specs, 10 appear in a stale record here.
   - `grid-file-upload` appears in none: `conditional-rules-grid` dropped its record at revision 8 (#24752).
   - `studio-editor` does appear in an item, though in no `automated.ref`: `record-page-roundtrip`'s stale `why`, `acceptance[1].verify` and `source[1]`.

## Acceptance notes

- `records-forms.crud-roundtrip` `acceptance[4].verify` still says `record-history-display.spec.ts` pins the contract "on showcase Project". At `0b36ffa` the spec drives `showcase_account`, and it no longer exercises booleans or datetimes, which `auditHistoryDisplay.test.ts` pins (objectui#13132 R5). The item is outside this claim, so this is noted here and not edited. Carrier: #24579.
- `studio-authoring.first-run-loop` `acceptance[0].verify` still says F1 "targets testids package-id-input / package-name-input that no source file declares". At `0b36ffa`, F1 creates the package through the Studio surface's switcher (`package-form-id-input`, `studio-pkg-chip`), so that note no longer describes the spec. The item is outside this claim. Carrier: #24579.
- `studio-authoring.record-page-roundtrip` acceptance[1]: `studio-editor.spec.ts` asserts the clause's picker (Card, Section, Record details) carrier-neutrally, on a copy of `showcase_project_workspace`. Adding it to the ref would widen the ref, which this round's ruling forbids, so it is left for a later theme-B pass. Carrier: #24579.
- `records-forms.master-detail-atomic-save`: `form-view-subforms.spec.ts` also asserts the batch's parent op with a `{$ref: 0}` child and the computed amount in the payload. The ref keeps only acceptance[4], as the ruling requires. Carrier: #24579.
- Neither the README nor `check-platform-checklist.mjs` gives `stale` any schema; the validator checks only `automated.ref`.

## Verification

**Editing.** Every area-file edit went through a scripted span editor that never re-serialises a file. It splices only the declared value spans, then re-parses and asserts four things:

- the document equals the old one with the declared ops applied;
- every other item and every top-level key is value-equal;
- each edited item's changed leaf paths are a subset of its declared fields, plus `revision` and the one new history row;
- the text outside the edited items' spans is byte-identical.

All three files passed, against 18 + 33 + 39 unedited items.

**Merge.** `origin/main` `b3fc122f07` was merged at `647dfb355c`, cleanly. PR #24850 had merged by then (10:48:41Z) and touched only `cli.json`, `access-security.json` and `approvals.json`; `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD 19eb546d9c` (its head) → exit 0.
